newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX shrugs off U.S. rate rise at start.
newsitem.headline: German DAX shrugs off U.S. rate rise at start.

text.p: Germany's DAX index moved ahead at start of trade on Wednesday, cancelling out pre-bourse losses after a widely-expected rise in a key U.S. interest rate that nonetheless took the Dow lower overnight.

Early dollar gains in Europe were seen positive for German export-sensitive stocks and the market also benefited from a positive reaction to 1996 business details from the country's largest bank, Deutsche Bank.
The DAX-30 index of leading shares rose 52.29, 1.56 percent to 3,401.43 in early trade, catching up with the post-rally that occurred on Tuesday and further gains in electronic trade today.

Early dealer fears that the market could go into reverse after Deutsche numbers did not materialise after the bank reported group pre-tax profit of 4.9 billion marks compared to 3.6 billion last year.
Deutsche shares rose 2.50 marks to 93.75 as the bank was also optimistic on its outlook for 1997.
Utility Veba also pulled back most of its early losses after its said 1996 group pre-tax profit rose 16 percent to 4.44 billion marks.
Its shares traded two pfennigs higher at 98.70 after earlier having fallen to 98.15 in IBIS electronic trade.
Thyssen was again among the top loss-leaders on continued reaction to the cancelled takeover bid by Krupp, which is due to make way for a steel joint venture between the two.
Thyssen shares fell to a low of 367.50 before later recovering to 2.00 marks lower at 373.50.
Car-maker BMW rose 70 marks to 1,294 on continued positive reaction to more 1996 business details given at a news conference on Tuesday.
